reader_situation: Someone hosting Thanksgiving with a frozen turkey wants to know what day it has to go into the fridge, and what to do if they're late or it's still icy.
direct_answer: Plan on one day of fridge thawing for every 4 pounds (Butterball's rule; Montana State Extension's general rule is 24 hours per 5 pounds), so a 16-pound turkey needs about 4 days and a 20-pound turkey about 5. Once thawed, cook raw poultry within 1 to 2 days. If you're late, thaw in cold water at about 30 minutes per pound with the water changed every 30 minutes and cook it right away, or cook from frozen, which takes about 50% longer.
consensus: Thaw in the refrigerator, about 24 hours per 4-5 pounds.
Cold water thawing takes about 30 minutes per pound with water changed every 30 minutes.
A turkey can be cooked from frozen; it takes longer.
gaps: The two published rates differ: Butterball says at least one day per 4 lb, Montana State Extension says at least 24 hours per 5 lb. Schedule with the 4-lb rule; the difference becomes a built-in cushion that still lands inside the 1-2 day window for thawed poultry.

Thawed is not a fresh start: Montana State Extension says thawed poultry stays safe in the fridge 1-2 days before cooking, matching USDA's raw poultry window; Butterball's page says to use the turkey within four days of thawing, so go with the shorter federal and extension window.

The fridge itself may be too warm: Ohio State food safety researchers report 43% of observed homes had a refrigerator above 41°F, and only 4-9% of fridges had a thermometer; FDA says keep it at 40°F or below and that few refrigerator controls show actual temperatures.

Cold-water details: Butterball says thaw breast side down in the unopened wrapper fully submerged, change the water every 30 minutes, and rotate the bird if it can't be fully submerged; Montana State says food thawed this way must be cooked immediately.
Fridge-thaw details: Butterball says breast side up, in the unopened wrapper, on a tray, fridge at 40°F or below.
Cooking from frozen takes about 50% longer (Montana State Extension); the 165°F minimum applies to whole and stuffed poultry (FDA).
Only fridge-thawed food can be refrozen without cooking (Montana State Extension; USDA registry).

evidence.detail: Allow at least one day of thawing for every 4 lbs of turkey. Keep the refrigerator at 40°F or below. Thaw breast side up in the unopened wrapper on a tray. Use within four days of thawing. Don't thaw at room temperature.
evidence.source_title: How to Thaw a Turkey | Butterball

evidence.detail: Cold water: breast side down, unopened wrapper, fully submerged; about 30 minutes per pound; change the water every 30 minutes; if not fully submerged, rotate every 30 minutes.
evidence.source_title: How to Thaw a Turkey | Butterball

evidence.claim: Extension fridge thaw rate, thawed window, refreezing
evidence.detail: Frozen foods require at least one day (24 hours) to thaw for every 5 pounds of weight. After thawing, ground meat, stew meat, poultry, and seafood stay safe in the refrigerator for 1-2 days before cooking. Foods thawed in the refrigerator may be refrozen without cooking.
evidence.source_title: Safe Thawing Practices | Montana State University Extension

evidence.claim: Extension cold water, microwave, cooking from frozen
evidence.detail: Cold water: leak-proof packaging, change the water every 30 minutes, a whole turkey takes about 30 minutes per pound; if thawed completely, cook immediately. Microwave-thawed food must be cooked right away. Cooking frozen food takes about 50% longer than fully thawed or fresh food.
evidence.source_title: Safe Thawing Practices | Montana State University Extension

evidence.claim: Safe minimum cooking temperature and thawing methods
evidence.detail: Poultry (ground, parts, whole, and stuffed): 165°F measured with a food thermometer. Don't thaw food on the counter; thaw in the refrigerator, in cold water, or in the microwave; food thawed in cold water or the microwave should be cooked right away. Refrigerate perishables within 2 hours (1 hour above 90°F).
Keep the refrigerator at 40°F or below and the freezer at 0°F. Few refrigerator controls show actual temperatures, so use a freestanding appliance thermometer and check it often.
evidence.source_title: Refrigerator Thermometers: Cold Facts about Food Safety | FDA

evidence.detail: Almost half (43%) of observed homes had a refrigerator that was too warm (>41°F). Just 4-9% of domestic refrigerators were observed to have a thermometer. Keep the home refrigerator at or below 40°F as measured with a thermometer.
evidence.source_title: Nobody likes cold, including bacteria | Ohio State University Food Safety

original_asset.spec: Thanksgiving thaw schedule by weight (12-24 lb) using Butterball's 1 day per 4 lb, rounded up, with the 'into the fridge by' day for a Thursday cook, the Montana 5-lb-rule finish as a cushion check against the 1-2 day thawed window, and a cold-water time column (30 min/lb).

cautions: Never thaw on the counter; 2-hour rule (registry).
Cold-water or microwave thawed turkey must be cooked immediately and cooked before refreezing (registry).
Safety is time and temperature, not smell (registry).
Cook to 165°F measured with a thermometer, including stuffing.
